result.result:
MV TORMAR SPRING (SIM-0002), in ballast from Rotterdam to Sept-Iles (ETA ~30 Jan 20:00), was last reported on 23 Jan making 12 knots with wind and sea increasing from the west.

The 24 Jan 00z forecast along her remaining route shows heavy weather on several stretches, starting 24 Jan 1200 UTC: first to ~26 Jan 0100 (wind up to Beaufort 7, seas 6.2 m), then a brief 26 Jan 1500-2100 spell (Beaufort 6, seas 4.4 m), a more marked 27 Jan 2100–28 Jan 0600 stretch (wind up to Beaufort 9, seas 5.5 m), and lighter 28–29 Jan seas up to 4.6 m on the bow.

Recommendation: write nothing to the Master. The office already advised him on 22 Jan (heavy weather 23 Jan 0400–26 Jan 0300 UTC, up to Beaufort 12 / 9.9 m, which he acknowledged), and the new run shifts the worst timing slightly later and is somewhat weaker, not new or more severe. He already has the warning and the heavy-weather routing window. An internal voyage note has been filed marking the 27 Jan overnight (and 28–29 Jan seas) as expected bad-weather days to be set aside from performance assessment; this is for office records only and need not be passed to the Master.
